lead.headline: Kushner meets Hamas chief in Cairo before Netanyahu talks
lead.dek: Hamas would disarm and Israeli forces withdraw. Netanyahu rejected the plan last week.
body: U.S. negotiator Jared Kushner met Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo on Sunday for more than two hours, seeking the group's commitment to a 15-point American road map for Gaza. Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish officials attended with envoy Steve Witkoff.

The plan would have Hamas hand its weapons to a Palestinian technocratic committee while Israeli forces halt attacks and withdraw, with an international force between them. Hamas said it wants Israel pulled back to the yellow line before a 14-day negotiating period opens.

Kushner, Tony Blair and Board of Peace director Nickolay Mladenov meet Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday. Netanyahu rejected the road map last week, saying Israel will not leave any position until Hamas is disarmed.

briefs.headline: Indiana flood deaths rise to 7 as Trump clears disaster aid
briefs.summary: Storms since Aug. 11 have killed at least seven. The White River crested above 24 feet at Anderson, past the 1913 record.

briefs.headline: Four states take Meta to trial over children's safety
briefs.summary: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey say the apps were built to addict children. The trial opens this week in Oakland.

briefs.headline: Lake Powell falls to its lowest level on record
briefs.summary: The reservoir hit 3,519.91 feet Saturday, under the April 2023 record and about 30 feet above where Glen Canyon Dam stops generating.

briefs.headline: Trump orders joint drills with South Korea cut back
briefs.summary: Trump told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to cut drills he called costly and hostile to North Korea. Ulchi Freedom Shield involves 18,000 troops.

briefs.headline: Thieves take Antonello works from a Sicilian museum
briefs.summary: A double-sided panel and three polyptych sections, valued at up to 80 million euros, were cut from the MuMe museum in Messina on Sunday night.

briefs.headline: Hichilema leads Zambia count as opposition alleges a raid
briefs.summary: The president had nearly 59% of votes counted, rival Brian Mundubile about a third. EU observers called the vote skewed to the incumbent.

briefs.headline: Falling electric pole kills 7 at a Bihar temple
briefs.summary: The pole came down at the Ashok Dham temple in Lakhisarai during Shravan, electrocuting worshippers and setting off a crush.

briefs.headline: Storms drop nearly a foot of rain on the Kanawha Valley
briefs.summary: Gauges read 11.8 inches near Eskdale, 6 to 10 from Kincaid to Danese. High water damaged U.S. 60 at Kanawha Falls and washed out CSX track near Pratt.

briefs.headline: Pratt & Whitney lands a $1B engine contract at Bridgeport
briefs.summary: The nine-year deal covers overhauls of PT6A-68 engines for military T-6 trainers at Bridgeport, where about 500 people work.

regional.item: Crews made water rescues on Garrison Avenue and Valley Road Sunday night as Elk Twomile Creek left its banks.

fishing.line: 4620 cfs and rising, up from 179 a day ago - blown out. Stay on the bank.

briefs.headline: Cheap heart drug cuts hospital admissions by a quarter
briefs.summary: A 1,000-patient trial across 43 Dutch centers found low-dose digoxin cut heart-failure admissions 25%. It costs under 10 cents a day.

briefs.headline: Collider data points to a gluon junction inside protons
briefs.summary: The STAR detector logged about twice as many baryons as expected, evidence a Y-shaped gluon knot carries baryon number, not the quarks.

briefs.headline: Sharp wrinkles turn graphene into an electrical switch
briefs.summary: Folds narrower than a nanometer separated charge up to 10 million times more strongly than larger systems. Sharpness beat height.

briefs.headline: COVID wakes dormant viruses in hospitalized patients
briefs.summary: A study of 1,154 patients at 20 hospitals found 11 viruses reactivating within 40 days. Inflammation, not immune suppression, was the trigger.
